What is the best Ghost CMS alternative?

It depends on which part of Ghost the CMS has to replace. If you want Ghost's hosted, distraction-free editing without running a server or paying $249/mo for yoursite.com/blog, Superblog is the closest match at $49/mo with the technical SEO automated. If you need the widest possible plugin and theme ecosystem and have someone to maintain it, WordPress is the deeper CMS. If your writers are engineers, Hashnode fits the workflow, though custom domains now require its $5/mo Pro tier. Self-hosted Ghost remains free if your team can operate it.

What is the Ghost blogging platform used for? [...] Is there a free Ghost alternative?

Several. WordPress, Hugo, and Jekyll are free and open source, though all three need a developer and a host. Medium, Substack, and Hashnode have free tiers, but each trades something for it: Medium and Substack keep you off your own domain path, and Hashnode moved custom domains into its paid tier in June 2026. Free costs you either engineering time or domain authority.

Ghost vs WordPress: which is better for SEO? [...] ## Ghost CMS Alternative: The Editor Without the Membership Stack

A lot of people searching for a Ghost CMS alternative are not trying to escape Ghost's writing experience. They like it. What they don't want is the rest of the package: a server to patch, a member portal and billing system they will never switch on, and a $249/mo bill to put posts on their own domain path.

If that describes you, the shortlist is narrower than the full list above. You want a hosted editor that keeps the distraction-free feel, publishes to a domain you control, and does the technical SEO without a plugin directory. Three of these platforms qualify:

If you love Ghost's creator monetization model but want lower cost or simpler setup, Beehiiv is the strongest move for serious newsletter publishers — especially once your revenue grows beyond $430/month, where Beehiiv's 0% cut becomes more economical than Substack's 10%. Substack is the right choice if you want the simplest possible path to a paid subscriber relationship with built-in discovery.

If you are in the HubSpot ecosystem and want your blog, CRM, and lead capture fully connected, HubSpot CMS makes sense despite the higher cost.

If you want maximum flexibility and have the technical resources to use it, WordPress gives you more control than any other platform on this list as a full-featured open source Ghost CMS alternative. [...] Editor's rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.3 / 5 · View on G2 →

WordPress powers over 43 percent of all websites and has the largest plugin and theme ecosystem of any platform. It is the most established open source Ghost CMS alternative — free to self-host, with a community of tens of millions of developers and 60,000+ plugins.

The tradeoff is maintenance. WordPress is the number one target for hackers and requires ongoing updates, plugin management, security monitoring, and performance optimization. Out of the box it does not match Ghost's speed. With the right hosting and configuration it can, but that takes real work from someone technical. ### Best for B2B content teams and SEO growth: Typeflo

Editor's rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.8 / 5 — Best for SEO and GEO-native publishing

Typeflo is built for exactly the type of team Ghost CMS has moved away from. Where Ghost optimises for creator monetization, Typeflo optimises for organic growth and lead generation.

The most immediate practical difference is subdirectory hosting. Typeflo offers it from $19 per month — Ghost Pro charges $199 for the same feature on its Business plan. For any business blog that needs to sit at yourcompany.com/blog to consolidate domain authority, that pricing gap is hard to ignore.
